Accounts.reason: Records carry their company; so the contract must only return stored records.

content.statement: Users are accounts of a company, records are contacts and deals, and sharing is a table of shares.
content.why: A record belongs to the company stored on it, and a user to the company of their account. This trusts the record, so ReadContract requires returned records to be the stored ones; it also trusts the account, which authentication provides (not modelled).
substitutions: sharedWith := (r: CrmRecord, t: TenantId) => shares.value.contains(Share(r.id, t))

  to : TenantId

ReadApi.reason: Users only see records through searches; revisit if we add exports.

content.statement: Records are shown only as query results, and a query returns only records the user may see.
content.why: Users find records by searching, so what a user sees is what their queries return. abs: a user is shown a record when some query of theirs returns it.

sources.spec: run => forall((u: User.T, q: Query.T) => run(u, q).forall(r => visible(u, r)))
sources.abs: run => (u, r) => exists((q: Query.T) => run(u, q).contains(r))

uses: fun (u : User) (r : Record) => (((owner r) = (tenantOf u)) ∨ (sharedWith r (tenantOf u)))

ReadContract.reason: Covers search by id, by kind and everything, as the idea lists.

content.statement: A search returns stored records only, each of the user's company or shared with it.
content.why: Accounts, stated for one call. A returned record must be one of the stored records, so an implementation cannot relabel another company's record as the user's.

sources.post: (user, query, result) => result.forall(r => store.value.contains(r) && (r.tenant == user.tenant || shares.value.contains(Share(r.id, user.tenant))))

examples: expect (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), Everything) ⇒ ::(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Deal, "Acme deal"), List())  given store = ::(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Deal, "Acme deal"), ::(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact"), List())), shares = List()  — Ann lists everything she can see: Acme's deal

expect (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), ById(2)) ⇒ List()  given store = ::(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Deal, "Acme deal"), ::(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact"), List())), shares = List()  — Globex's contact is not shared with Acme

reject (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), ById(2)) ⇒ ::(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact"), List())  given store = ::(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Deal, "Acme deal"), ::(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact"), List())), shares = List()  — another company's record is never returned

reject (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), Everything) ⇒ ::(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("acme"), Contact, "Globex contact"), List())  given store = ::(CrmRecord(1, TenantId("acme"), Deal, "Acme deal"), ::(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact"), List())), shares = List()  — a record relabelled as Acme's is not a stored record

expect (Account("ann@acme", TenantId("acme")), OfKind(Contact)) ⇒ ::(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact"), List())  given store = ::(CrmRecord(2, TenantId("globex"), Contact, "Globex contact"), List()), shares = ::(Share(2, TenantId("acme")), List())  — Globex shared its contact with Acme, so Ann finds it by kind

TenantIsolation.reason: Isolation between companies is the promise of a shared CRM.

content.statement: A user sees a record only if it belongs to their company or was shared with their company.
content.why: Isolation between companies is what the idea says must hold. Companies, users, records and sharing are left open.

sources.spec: shows => forall((u: User.T, r: Record.T) => shows(u, r) ==> visible(u, r))

uses: fun (u : User) (r : Record) => (((owner r) = (tenantOf u)) ∨ (sharedWith r (tenantOf u)))
content.idea:
# CRM

Many companies use one CRM. Each company's users manage contacts and deals.
A user may see a record only if it belongs to their company, or if the record's
company has shared it with theirs. Users find records by id, by kind, or list
everything they can see.
